data.description:
## The defect (proven, not inferred)

`tests/unit/test_anthropic_lazy_import_isolation_heldout.py` hand-rolls a nested pytest launch
with **no `--basetemp`**, so its child sessions allocate into the SHARED numbered temp root and
destroy other sessions' roots.

`tests/_nested_pytest.py` states the invariant and why it exists: omitting `--basetemp` "lets a
child clean another run's shared numbered temp root", and it "arrived as three separate bugs
before this module existed". This test bypasses that module entirely.

Demonstrated by one serial run of the file, diffing `pytest-of-joeoakhart/`:

```
--- created ---   pytest-2313 pytest-2315 pytest-2316 pytest-2317
--- DELETED ---   pytest-2304 pytest-2310 pytest-2311 pytest-2312
```

Four nested sessions allocated into the shared root and destroyed four other sessions' roots.

## Why the existing guard does not catch it — the more important half

`tests/unit/test_nested_pytest_uniqueness.py` detects violations by scanning for the argv triple
`(sys.executable, "-m", "pytest")`. This module spells the same operation as
`(sys.executable, "-c", <script that calls pytest.main>)`.

So it is an **unmarked, undetected violation**: the convention exists, the guard exists, and the
guard's detection shape is narrower than the behaviour it guards. Any future test that drives
pytest through `python -c` gets the same free pass. That is the durable defect — the single test
is just the instance that revealed it.

This is the same family as several other findings in this repo where the CHECK was narrower than
the thing it checked: a CI parity test edited by the very commit that diverged the lanes without
noticing, a drift gate that died on formatting before it ever ran `plan`, an alarm audit that
partitioned on two values of `treat_missing_data` and could not see a third.

## Why it plausibly explains a real flake class

A nested-pytest spawner is DOUBLY exposed: the child's own leak guard can return a non-zero exit,
which surfaces in the parent as a bare `assert completed.returncode == 0` — a failure whose
message says nothing about the actual cause.

A same-family flake was observed while investigating (1 of 3 iterations): `_no_repo_root_leaks`
failing an innocent test on a transient `.rebar/.hlc.state.*.tmp`. That hit a different module
(`test_subprocess_env_repr_security.py`) and the guard's own docstring notes a concurrent external
`rebar` write is indistinguishable there — so it shows the SHAPE is achievable but is not proof
that it caused ticket `undesirous-undiseased-zebu`. Recorded as suggestive, not conclusive.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] AC1 - `test_anthropic_lazy_import_isolation_heldout.py` no longer allocates into the shared
      numbered temp root. Route it through `run_nested_pytest`, or pass `--basetemp` under
      `tmp_path` with a reasoned `# nested-pytest-ok:` marker. Prove by diffing
      `pytest-of-<user>/` across a run and showing NO other session's root is deleted.
- [ ] AC2 - The uniqueness guard detects a `pytest.main(...)` payload driven through
      `python -c`, not only the `python -m pytest` argv triple. Prove by pointing the guard at the
      pre-fix form of this file and observing it FAIL.
- [ ] AC3 - Defect-seeded: reverting AC1 makes AC2's guard go RED. A guard that cannot distinguish
      the fixed form from the broken one has not been shown to work — which is precisely how the
      current guard came to miss this.
- [ ] AC4 - A sweep records whether any OTHER test drives pytest through a form the guard cannot
      see. List what was scanned. If others exist, each gets a disposition (fixed here, or its own
      ticket) — silence is not a disposition.

## Non-goals

Not fixing the order-dependent failure reported in `undesirous-undiseased-zebu` — that was
investigated and NOT REPRODUCED, and this ticket does not claim to explain it. Not changing the
nested-pytest convention itself, only its enforcement and this one violator.
data.title: A nested-pytest launch driven through python -c evades the uniqueness guard and destroys other sessions' shared temp roots: proven 4-created/4-deleted, and the guard only detects the python -m pytest form
